sections.text: Watch this reply sit here. It is written, it is right, and it goes nowhere until somebody presses the button.
You are choosing a tool that writes what your customers read. The feature list says what it produces. It never says where you sit.
A person can sit in three places. Before the draft, which is a form. After it is sent, which is an apology. Or here, in between.
Same task, twice. First with the tool set to send. Now set to hold. One queue, one draft, one name on it, a button nobody has pressed.
We counted our own. Twenty-five named steps from a video coming in to the job being finished, and one place where it waits for a person. That person struck out nine of the last twenty-three.
So the question for the sales call is not which model is inside. It is: show me where my draft waits.
If that screen does not exist, do not buy it for anything a customer reads. Send this to whoever signs.

strategy.audience: Non-technical small-business leader, AI level 0-6 of 10 (POSITIONING.md §4): an owner, operations lead or team lead in a 5-50 person company responsible for one repeated process. Specifically the person choosing a tool that will write or send something a customer reads.
strategy.concept: One question replaces a feature comparison: does the tool stop and wait for a person before anything leaves the company. We show the same task run twice, full-frame and one after the other - once set to send, once set to hold - and then count the same gate in our own pipeline, where twenty-five named steps run unattended and one waits for a person who struck out nine of the last twenty-three plans.

filter.ai_boundary: The tool drafts and queues. A named person releases. Nothing addressed to somebody outside the company leaves without that person having seen it on a screen.
filter.friction: Feature lists say what the tool can produce and never say where the person sits, so the approval step is discovered after the tool is already inside the workflow and something has already gone out unread.
filter.next_action: Open the tool you are evaluating, find the setting that holds output for review, and if it does not exist, do not buy it for outward-facing work.
filter.process: Buying or switching a tool that produces outward-facing text - replies, quotes, summaries, posts, anything a customer or a supplier will read with the company's name on it.

strategy.objective: Get one viewer to open the tool they are evaluating, look for the setting that holds output for review, and refuse the purchase for outward-facing work if that setting does not exist.
strategy.promise: One question that replaces a feature comparison, and the exact screen to ask for before you sign.
strategy.rationale: Exactly one reel in the 266-reel analysed corpus states the boundary out loud, and it does so as a throwaway objection beat inside a tool promotion. Making the boundary the subject is unrepresented. The visual shape is the one the data supports: A>SCREEN>A carries median share_rate 0.0213 against 0.0140 (p=0.00076, I-11) and opening on the screen is worth roughly half again the forwarding rate (I-09).

traceability.evidence_summary: Exactly one reel in the 266-reel analysis-ready corpus states an AI boundary out loud, and it does so as a throwaway objection beat inside a tool promotion (DczDlj4qQjI, beat B3, 56.6 saves per 1 000): making the boundary the subject is unrepresented. Our own gate count is real and checkable: twenty-five named stages in engine/SPEC.md §3, one place that waits for a person, and that person struck 9 of the 23 plans the pipeline produced across three weeks. The visual grammar follows the two strongest findings we have - opening on a screen carries median share_rate 0.0213 against 0.0140 with a creator-normalised correlation of +0.285, p=0.00025 (I-09), and the A>SCREEN>A run carries the same 0.0213 against 0.0140 at p=0.00076 across 39 reels and 32 creators (I-11). The topic reference Dbi-yxNgrhG holds the reference pool's highest share rate at 58.4 per 1 000, fourth in the analysis-ready corpus on a bounded-controls-in-a-familiar-system shape, and DTCOU9DkRTG (52.0x lift, ungated) supplies the imperative opening over an already-running screen.
traceability.original_synthesis: The subject is the pause itself, which nothing in the corpus treats as the subject. The gate count is ours, dated and reproducible from engine/SPEC.md §3 and data/radar.db, and it is offered as an experiment rather than as a client result. The three-positions frame - before the draft, after the send, in between - is ours and is not in any reference.
traceability.why_better_than_generic: A generic AI script would list five tools with a 'human in the loop' bullet and call the boundary a best practice. This one replaces the feature comparison with a single screen the viewer can ask to see, films the two runs full-frame and sequentially rather than as the split screen the corpus over-uses and under-rewards (I-10), names our own gate ratio instead of a principle, and refuses to claim that the gate prevents anything, because we have not measured it.
